category_specific_evidence: np.percentile(np.ones(10, dtype="float32"), np.float64(3)) should return float64 because q is float64, but gh-29105 returned float32 by incorrectly letting the array dtype win.
test_q_weak_promotion asserts float32 result for float32 input with q in [0.5, 1] under interpolating methods.
test_q_strong_promotion asserts float64 result for float32 input with np.float64(0.5) under interpolating methods; the comment says discrete methods keep the original dtype.
The fix defers casting to the input dtype to the end of computation via weak_q, in nanpercentile and _nanquantile_1d.

reproduction_risks: The discrepancy depends on whether q is a Python float/int (weak) or np.float64 (strong), and on whether the method is interpolating or discrete.
Longdouble inputs previously used higher precision for q computation; this is no longer done after the fix, which is a known side effect.
